title: The Shell Company
logline: When both of Lily's Career Day parents cancel, she drafts the gang to present to her kindergarten class, and one gold star sticker per kid turns four grown-ups into bitter rivals. Ted's lecture dies, Marshall's environmental law becomes a Bigfoot story, Robin is upstaged by her own news clip, and Barney, for whom 'Please' doesn't work on a five-year-old, finally has to explain what he does.
coldOpen: Kids, to this day, the only people on Earth who know what your Uncle Barney does for a living are twenty-two former members of Aunt Lily's kindergarten class.

guests.name: Dale Brophy
guests.role: Jaden's dad, the FDNY firefighter who cancelled on Career Day because of a fire. Seen only in Robin's live news clip, where he waves to his son on camera with the bodega goat he just rescued and cheerfully talks over Robin's entire report

scenes.summary: The night before Career Day, Lily's dentist and firefighter parents both cancel, so she drafts the gang. Five-year-olds are honest; each kid gives one gold star; the fewest stickers chaperones the aquarium. Ted brings slides, Robin is on TV, Barney plans to say 'Please'. Marshall plays a five-year-old asking Barney 'why' until Barney blurts out his deepest fear. Button: Marshall asks for a juice box.

beats.line: It started the night before Career Day, with a phone call.
No, totally fine, Doctor Kessler. Feel better.
That was my pediatric dentist. She has the flu. Career Day is tomorrow, and I have zero parents.
Baby, what about the firefighter? Jaden's dad?
He cancelled. Because of a fire.
That does sound like his job.
Twenty-two kids were promised grown-ups with jobs, Robin. The fire can wait.
Which is why you four are presenting.
Lily, I lecture graduate students twice a week. I think I can handle a few five-year-olds.
Grad students are polite, Ted. Five-year-olds are honest. Last year a tax attorney presented, and a little girl asked him to stop.
I'm in. Kids love me. I'm basically a bouncy castle with a law degree.
I'm on TV, Ted. To a five-year-old, I'm basically Elmo.
Barney, you too. And you have to tell them what you do.
Please.
That doesn't work on five-year-olds. You say please to a five-year-old, they say thank you and wait for a juice box.
Afterwards, every kid gets one gold star sticker to give their favorite grown-up.
So it's a competition.
No, Ted. It's a celebration of all kinds of work.
And whoever gets the fewest stickers chaperones our field trip to the aquarium.
How bad can an aquarium be?
Twenty-two five-year-olds. One shark tunnel. Last year's chaperone still can't look at a penguin.
Robin, you're going down. Architecture is literally building blocks. I'm bringing slides.
Slides. For five-year-olds. I've already won.
Barney, let's practice. I'll be the five-year-old. I'm incredible at it.
He is. He once asked a park ranger why for forty minutes.
Mister Barney, what's your job?
I'm a senior executive at a global financial institution.
Why?
To make money.
Why?
It's called capitalism, Marshall! Look it up!
I can't read. Why?
Because nobody loves me unless I'm winning!
Can I have a juice box?

scenes.summary: Career Day in the school auditorium; the kids sit on the carpet at the fourth wall. Ted's lecture dies: part one of eleven, a buttress that Barney turns into a chant, and Hazel's loose tooth (runner 1). Penny calls out the speech from her birthday. Marshall loses them on wetlands, then wins them with Bigfoot, who now has a lawyer, and scares them out of recess. Button: Robin tells them Bigfoot isn't real.

beats.line: The next morning, in the school auditorium, we faced the toughest crowd of our lives.
Friends, criss-cross applesauce! Our first grown-up makes buildings. Say good morning to Mister Ted!
Good morning! Hi, I'm Ted Mosby, architect.
My grad students at least pretend to write that down.
So! Who here lives in a building? Everybody! And who knows who designed it?
Nobody. That's okay. Let's start at the very beginning. Ancient Greece.
Part one of eleven. The column.
beats.title: Architecture: A Love Story

beats.line: Dad, you gave this exact speech at my sixth birthday party.
Penny, you asked for a castle cake. I gave you context.
And then the Gothic cathedral gave us the flying buttress.
No. Buttress. It's a support structure. It's not funny.
Buttress!
Barney! Great. Now they're chanting it.
That's three stickers. Minimum.
A question! Yes, you with the pigtails? Your tooth is loose.
Great! Actually, a tooth is a lot like a load-bearing column—
She's gone, Ted. Hazel's showing it to the hamster.
Thank you, Mister Ted! That was so many words!
Hi, guys! I'm Marshall. I'm an environmental lawyer. I protect nature from people who want to hurt it.
Like a superhero? Yes! Exactly like a superhero. With more paperwork.
For instance, last month I filed a fourteen-page motion about wetland runoff in northern New Jersey.
Lily, I'm losing them. Two of them are lying face down.
Animals, Marshall. Talk about animals.
Right! The forest! Who lives in the forest? Bears. Owls. Deer.
Marshall. Don't.
And a seven-foot hairy gentleman who just wants to be left alone.
They call him Bigfoot.
You, in the dinosaur shirt. Have I seen him? Not yet. But I've seen where he's been.
Does he have a lawyer? He does now.
He's campaigning with a cryptid. That has to be against the rules.
There are no rules against Bigfoot, Ted. I checked. Lawyered.
Is he outside right now? Buddy, he could be anywhere.
Marshall, recess is in five minutes.
But he's definitely in Canada! Very far away. Super cold. Nobody goes there.
Too late. Nobody's going to recess, and Hunter wants Bigfoot at his birthday party.
Relax. I've got this. Kids need the truth.
Kids. Bigfoot isn't real.
Robin! They're five!

scenes.summary: After a juice break, Robin calls Bigfoot a developing story and rolls her best clip, the fire that made Jaden's dad cancel. The clip shows him rescuing a goat, and the room is his. Hazel's tooth is still loose (runner 2). Barney's 'Please' gets silence, the why-chain starts, then Hazel's tooth comes out (runner 3) and Barney explains his job: the tooth fairy. The kids nod; the grown-ups are more lost than ever. Sticker chart: Jaden's dad wins without showing up, Robin gets zero, Ted ties the hamster.

beats.line: After an emergency juice break, Robin tried again.
Okay. Correction. Bigfoot is a developing story.
I'm a news anchor. I tell people what's happening in the world, even when it's scary.
You. Am I famous? In Canada. Briefly. Next question.
Let me show you my best work. This morning I covered a three-alarm fire in Queens. Lily, roll it.

beats.label: Metro News One, live, that morning

beats.line: Robin Scherbatsky, live in Queens, where a bodega fire is finally under control.
Hi, Jaden! Daddy saved a goat!
Sir, we're live.
His name is Mister Pickles. He lives in the bodega. Nobody knows why.
Officials say the cause of the fire is still under investigation.
It was Mister Pickles.
Yes, that's Jaden's dad. Everybody sit down. Jaden, you can stand. Just Jaden.
Questions about journalism? You. Can Mister Pickles come to school? No. Anyone with a question that isn't about the goat?
Hazel. Your tooth is even looser than it was during Mister Ted.
This just in. Hazel's tooth, still loose. More at eleven. Back to you, Hazel.
I've interviewed two prime ministers, Ted. I just lost a room to a goat.
Barney, what are you going to tell them you do?
Same thing I tell everyone.
Kids. I'm Barney. And what do I do?
Please.
Nothing? That kills at brunch.
They're waiting for the rest of the sentence.
Fine. I'm in senior management at a global bank, where I oversee strategic operations.
What's strategic? It means on purpose. What do I do on purpose? I go to meetings. I sign things.
Why? Oh no. Not why.
Don't say the thing about love.
Yes, Hazel? Your tooth just came out? Right now?
Hold it up high, Hazel. Everybody. What happens when you put a tooth under your pillow?
Money. Right. And how does a tooth turn into money?
Has anybody ever asked?
Exactly. That's my job.
Wait. Is he saying he's the tooth fairy?
No, Ted. He's saying the tooth fairy is a shell company.
And they all nodded. Every single one of them.
Any questions?
None. That's how you know it's working.
Okay, friends! Sticker time!
And the winner, with ten gold stars, is Jaden's dad.
beats.title: Career Day Gold Stars

beats.line: He wasn't even here! Those stickers are all on me!
They're for Jaden's dad, Robin. Legally, you're the courier.
At least somebody gave me one. Who was it?
Owen. He said you looked like you needed it.
Still. I beat Robin.
You tied with the hamster, Ted.
The hamster didn't even present!
He ran on his wheel the whole time. Very confident.

scenes.summary: That night the presenters lick their wounds. Barney's 'Please' still works on grown-ups. Lily brings the kids' drawings of their favorite grown-up: Ted in love with a building, Marshall holding hands with Bigfoot, Robin in a cape, Barney as the tooth fairy who was the only one who listened about Hazel's tooth. Lily sees her friends the way her class does (aww), then reveals all four are chaperoning the aquarium. Barney slips Hazel a hundred dollars. Future Ted: Hazel works at GNB now, and says 'Please.'

beats.line: Twenty-two children, Robin. And all they'll remember from architecture is the word buttress.
I've covered two hurricanes. I came in behind a hamster.
Lily's making me send a note home to twenty-two families, clarifying my position on Bigfoot.
What's your position?
Respectful, but open.
Well, I had a great day. Second place, and I finally explained my job.
To kindergartners. So explain it to us. What do you actually do?
Please.
Yeah, okay.
See? Still works on grown-ups.
I asked the class to draw their favorite grown-up from Career Day.
Let me guess. Twenty-two goats.
Only nine. The rest drew you guys.
Owen drew you next to a very tall building. He wrote, Mister Ted loves buildings more than anybody in the whole world.
He's five, and he gets me better than my last three girlfriends.
Priya drew you holding hands with Bigfoot. You both have briefcases.
He has representation.
Mia drew you in a cape. She says you're the lady who tells people the scary news, so they don't have to be scared.
That's actually the job.
And Hazel drew you as the tooth fairy. She wrote, Mister Barney was the only one who listened about my tooth.
Nailed it.
You know, I spend all day with five-year-olds and all night with you guys. Some nights I can't tell the difference.
But today my kids looked at you and saw a man who loves buildings, a giant who believes, a woman who isn't scared of anything.
And the tooth fairy.
And they were right. You all showed up at eight a.m. because I asked. You're the best grown-ups I know.
Which is why all four of you are chaperoning the aquarium on Friday.
Only the loser was supposed to go!
I needed four chaperones, Robin. There was never a loser.
That's evil.
That's kindergarten.
Barney, what did you do with Hazel's tooth?
Handled. Tonight she finds a crisp hundred-dollar bill under her pillow.
Barney, you can't give a five-year-old a hundred dollars!
I'm not. The tooth fairy is.
Kids, Hazel is twenty-three now. Last spring, she took a job at Goliath National Bank, working for your Uncle Barney.
I asked her what she does there. She just smiled and said, Please.
